rawCandidates.selectionReason: Direct beauty booking homepage pattern with treatment search, time/location filters, and strong above-fold intent.
Venue-detail structure shows how services, proof, media, and book-now actions can stack without losing booking focus.
High-energy wellness media system with central CTA card; useful as a photo-direction reference, not proof reference.
Editorial scheduling landing page with disciplined nav, testimonial row, and single memorable accent CTA.
Booking-product proof artifact can become a service-decision artifact without copying SaaS trust logos.
Reservation search pattern maps well to date/time/service decisions and localized booking intent.
Consult-first flow with calm split-section hierarchy; useful for new colour clients before booking service work.
Consultation CTA, bullet hierarchy, and rounded section transition help translate regulated-adjacent caution to salon claims.
Numbered how-it-works section offers a clear consultation process model without requiring fake results.
Service category menu overlay shows how to expose treatment choice without overwhelming the first viewport.
Service rows with duration, price, category tabs, and book buttons provide a useful menu model.
Single CTA in photo-led section demonstrates restraint, though imagery and claim style need rejection for this fixture.
Strong product-photo composition is useful as an anti-pattern for fake salon photography and as a layout contrast.
Large proof-stat section is useful only as a warning because this fixture has no outcome metrics.
Outcome-stat hero is a clear anti-reference for salon transformation claims and invented proof.
Photography concept proves the risk of imported editorial images overpowering source truth.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first decision a service-and-time decision, not a brand admiration moment.
Hero leads with the booking job, then exposes service/category detail below the fold.
Large quiet hero plus horizontal decision bar keeps one dominant action visible.
Search controls can collapse into a stacked mobile booking module.

bannedUses: Do not copy Fresha's marketplace brand, appointment-count proof, pastel gradient, or exact search component.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Proof, when present, sits beside service choice instead of becoming decorative social proof.
Media should prove place/service only when owner-supplied; otherwise use a service-led no-photo artifact.
A persistent book-now action belongs near the service menu, not only in the nav.
Each service row can become a service-specific booking or consultation path.

bannedUses: Do not invent venue photos, ratings, reviews, staff names, map details, or prices from the reference.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use one decisive accent for action; keep surrounding color restrained.
A central white action surface can sit over richer media without becoming a generic card stack.
Rounded media crops can create softness without making every section a card.
If photos are absent, replace the collage with owner-safe swatches, tools, service cards, or colour consultation artifacts.

bannedUses: Do not use stock model imagery, gym/wellness collage assets, ClassPass claims, or trial language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Oversized editorial serif headline can make a booking-focused page feel crafted rather than SaaS-generic.
Plain promise with a confident, useful booking outcome beats fluffy beauty language.
CTA button, proof row, and nav can be minimal if hierarchy is strong.
Depth should come from typographic scale and spacing first, not shadows everywhere.

bannedUses: Do not copy testimonial quotes, star ratings, yellow CTA treatment, or the scheduling-product claim.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Keep a small token set for border, surface, type scale, and one action color so variations stay controllable.
A static proof artifact or service ledger can replace heavy galleries until real imagery is approved.
The visible service/consultation structure should map to page metadata and agent-readable service facts.
Booking/date/service selectors need clear focus, selected, disabled, and empty states.

bannedUses: Do not use SaaS logo strips, Trustpilot badges, Google sign-in, or enterprise proof.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: The page can guide a visitor through service, timing, and contact choice without requiring a full app flow.
Date, duration, area, and service names must match the local market and owner-approved facts.
Search and booking controls need keyboard labels and touch targets, not just visual pills.
A short booking/enquiry module should capture the next action without inventing availability.

bannedUses: Do not use restaurant imagery, city skyline, marketplace inventory, or reservation-count proof.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Explain consultation as the safest first step before high-consideration work.
Claims that imply expertise, outcomes, or credentials must be withheld unless source-backed.
Any motion should clarify the consultation path, such as service-step reveal or selected-service transition.
Replace medical/provider proof with owner-approved process proof and service-menu proof.

bannedUses: Do not copy medical imagery, provider credentials, telehealth claims, or outcome language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use abstract service artifacts, swatches, and process tokens instead of fake before-and-after images.
Generous process spacing can slow down anxious service decisions without feeling empty.
Numbered steps should be clearer than decorative beauty icons for consultation flow.
Secondary CTAs can route to service detail while primary CTA stays consultation/book focused.

bannedUses: Do not copy healthcare process claims, treatment outcomes, portrait overlays, or medication/product graphics.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Large outcome-stat proof would create fake salon transformation claims.
Photo-led editorial composition depends on borrowed imagery and would violate the photo-free fixture constraint.
Dramatic dark entertainment palette does not match a consultation-led local salon decision.

remixDirection.summary: A consultation-first salon page with an editorial booking hero, service decision ladder, owner-safe swatch/proof artifact, and persistent service-specific booking path.
selectedMoves: Fresha-inspired booking decision bar, rebuilt as a source-backed consultation/service chooser.
SavvyCal-inspired editorial scale and single-action discipline.
Hers-inspired consultation process clarity, stripped of medical/outcome claims.
Fresha venue/service-menu logic for duration and service comparison.
No-photo visual system using colour swatches, service ledgers, and consultation cards.
explicitRejects: No invented reviews, ratings, stylists, salon interiors, before-and-after images, or transformation claims.
No marketplace appointment-count proof or SaaS logo-strip trust proof.
No exact layout copy from any shortlisted screen.
